scheme_name: Scheme of Death Benefit for Weavers & Artisans of West Bengal
description:
The Scheme of Death Benefit for Weavers and Artisans of West Bengal was launched by the Government of West Bengal on 1st January 2014. 

This initiative was aimed at providing financial assistance to the families of deceased weavers and artisans. 

The scheme recognizes the significant contributions of weavers and artisans to the cultural and economic fabric of the state. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to offer a financial safety net to the families of weavers and artisans who pass away. 

The government aims to alleviate the financial burden faced by these families during a time of loss. 

The scheme provides a one-time death benefit of ₹2 lakh to the eligible beneficiaries. 

This amount is intended to support the families in meeting immediate expenses following the death of the breadwinner. 

The scheme is specifically designed for weavers and artisans who are registered under the West Bengal Handloom and Textiles Department. 

To qualify for the benefits, the applicant must be a registered weaver or artisan. 

The eligibility criteria stipulate that the applicant must be a resident of West Bengal. 

The age limit for eligibility is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no upper age limits specified for the applicants. 

The income criteria for eligibility require that the annual income of the weaver or artisan should not exceed ₹1.5 lakh. 

This income limit is aimed at targeting the economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and designed to be user-friendly. 

Interested applicants must visit the official website of the West Bengal Handloom and Textiles Department. 

The application form can be downloaded from the website or obtained from local government offices. 

Applicants must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their identity and profession. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with the required documents. 

Required documents include a copy of the death certificate of the deceased weaver or artisan. 

Applicants must also provide proof of registration as a weaver or artisan. 

Additional documents may include identity proof such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The processing time for applications is typically around 30 days. 

Beneficiaries are notified through official communication once their application is approved. 

The death benefit amount is disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

This ensures that the funds are transferred securely and efficiently. 

The scheme is implemented by the West Bengal Handloom and Textiles Department. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the registration of weavers and artisans. 

They also handle the disbursement of benefits under this scheme. 

For any inquiries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the department at their official helpline number. 

The helpline number is available on the department's official website. 

The scheme has been instrumental in providing financial support to numerous families since its inception. 

As of October 2023, thousands of families have benefited from this initiative. 

The government continues to promote the scheme to ensure that more weavers and artisans are aware of the benefits available to them. 

Regular awareness campaigns are conducted across the state to inform potential beneficiaries. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from the community for its timely support. 

It has also been recognized as a vital step towards improving the livelihoods of weavers and artisans. 

The West Bengal government has allocated a significant budget for the implementation of this scheme. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, the allocation for the scheme was ₹50 crore. 

This budget is aimed at ensuring that the benefits reach all eligible families without delay. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the West Bengal government to uplift the handloom and handicraft sectors. 

These sectors are crucial for the state's economy and cultural heritage. 

The government is committed to enhancing the welfare of weavers and artisans through various schemes. 

The Scheme of Death Benefit is one of the key components of this commitment. 

The government also provides other forms of assistance such as skill development programs. 

These programs are designed to enhance the skills of weavers and artisans. 

The overall goal is to increase their income and improve their living standards. 

The Scheme of Death Benefit for Weavers and Artisans of West Bengal is a vital safety net. 

It ensures that families do not face financial hardships in the wake of losing their primary earners. 

The scheme exemplifies the government's dedication to supporting the traditional crafts of the state. 

The initiative is a testament to the importance of preserving the cultural heritage of West Bengal. 

In conclusion, the Scheme of Death Benefit for Weavers and Artisans of West Bengal is a significant welfare initiative. 

It provides essential financial support to families in need. 

The scheme is well-structured and accessible to eligible beneficiaries. 

The West Bengal government continues to work towards enhancing the welfare of its weavers and artisans. 

This scheme plays a crucial role in ensuring their financial security and dignity.
